title: Arsenal 0-2 Lyon: Brand and Dumornay book quarter-final place
subtitle: Lyon's place in the knockout rounds of the Women's Champions League is now confirmed, while Arsenal miss the chance to close in at the top.
paragraphs: Lyon booked their place in the Women's Champions League quarter-finals with a 2-0 win over Arsenal, who suffered their first loss in Europe this season.

Jule Brand put Lyon in front midway through the first half before Melchie Dumornay made sure of the victory before the hour to ensure they continue to keep pace with Barcelona at the top of the table.
Lyon dominated the first half, with Misa forced into an early save to keep out Vicki Becho at her near post.
Wendie Renard glanced a header wide before Tabitha Chawinga caused some panic as she dragged a low effort past the far post from the right of the box.
But Lyon got their reward for the fast start in the 24th minute when Lily Yohannes played in Becho on the right wing, and she picked out the unmarked Brand for a first-time finish at the near post.
Yohannes then found a pocket of space on the edge of the box, and she had Misa scrambling, but her whipped, curling strike flew just wide of the target.
Arsenal showed more of a threat in the second half, with Alessia Russo firing a snapshot against the Lyon defence.
But just as Arsenal started to gain some rhythm, Lyon dealt another blow when Marie-Antoinette Katoto held up Chawinga's left-sided cross to tee up Dumornay for an emphatic finish.
Katoto glanced a point-blank header wide shortly after before Dumornay forced a sharp reaction save out of Misa, who also got behind Selma Bacha's drilled effort to keep the deficit down for Arsenal.

Arsenal's form at the Emirates has been a cause for concern in the Women's Super League this season, but they had previously shaken that off in the Champions League at Meadow Park, winning both home games in the competition.
However, against a Lyon side who have been free-scoring this term, they fell short.

It should perhaps come as no surprise given Lyon are now unbeaten across the first five games, and are still yet to concede in the Champions League this season (along with Chelsea), while scoring 22 goals themselves.
Lyon blew Renee Slegers' side away in the first half, having 13 shots worth 1.39 expected goals (xG) while Arsenal managed just one off-target attempt worth 0.06 xG.
The Gunners only improved their total to 0.35 xG, and did not test Mala Grohs with any of their six efforts.

There was a point during the game when Lyon were top of the league table, but they were leapfrogged by the full-time whistle. Barcelona moved above them on goals scored after their 6-0 thumping of Servette, with Claudia Pina netting a hat-trick to also confirm the Blaugrana's place in the last eight.
Bayern Munich also registered a big win, beating Austria Wien 4-0 to move up to third, leaving them just two points behind Barcelona and Lyon. Arsenal have slipped down to eighth.
